subject.title: Multi-agent orchestration is unstable: concurrent agents add/config overwrites, session-lock failures, and detached child work

question: Should #43367 remain the canonical umbrella while focused session-lock, delivery, fallback-lane, and cancellation fixes land, or should maintainers replace it with narrower canonical issues now?
rationale: The report is valid, but the solution boundary spans core session ownership, durable delivery guarantees, provider failover behavior, and detached child cleanup, which requires maintainer intent before automation chooses an architecture.

options.title: Keep Umbrella And Land Focused Fixes
options.body: Keep #43367 open, require focused PRs or issues for each root cause, and close the umbrella only when the linked symptoms are fixed or explicitly split.

options.title: Promote Completion Isolation Design
options.body: Make #96975 the canonical product direction for metadata-only completion isolation and route remaining lock/fallback defects to separate owners.

options.title: Split By Failure Mode
options.body: Create or select one canonical tracker each for config writes, session locks, completion delivery, auth failover, and detached work, then close this umbrella after linking the evidence.

recommendation.title: Keep Umbrella And Land Focused Fixes
recommendation.body: Keep #43367 open, require focused PRs or issues for each root cause, and close the umbrella only when the linked symptoms are fixed or explicitly split.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining choice is mainly an architecture/product boundary decision across subagent delivery and session ownership, where steipete has the strongest history signal.
